tasks.title: envvar help for an empty value or a sequence
tasks.issue:
Help text and missing-option errors handle envvar badly when it is empty or a sequence.

For an option named --units with show_envvar=True:
- If envvar is None, "", or [], help should look like an option with no envvar. With no auto envvar prefix, the help contains the line "  --units TEXT". With auto envvar prefix WEATHER, the help contains "  --units TEXT  [env var: WEATHER_UNITS]".
- If the option is required and the user passes nothing, the error names every variable. envvar "UNITS" and envvar ["UNITS"] both produce: Missing option '--units' (env var: 'UNITS').
- envvar ["WEATHER_UNITS", "UNITS"] or ("WEATHER_UNITS", "UNITS") produces: Missing option '--units' (env var: 'WEATHER_UNITS', 'UNITS').
- An empty envvar produces: Missing option '--units'. There is no env var hint.

tasks.title: short help cuts abbreviations in the wrong place
tasks.issue:
make_default_short_help cuts a help string in the wrong place when a period is part of an abbreviation, or when the next sentence does not start with a capital letter.

Examples of the wanted short text:
- "Weigh apples vs. pears." at width 30 stays "Weigh apples vs. pears."
- "Weigh apples vs. pears and plums." at width 20 becomes "Weigh apples vs...."
- "123 567 9. aaaa bbb" at width 10 becomes "123 567..." because the text after the period is lowercase, so it is not a new sentence.
- "123 567 9. Aaaa bbb" at width 10 becomes "123 567 9."
- "Pick a fruit. 3 remain." at width 20 becomes "Pick a fruit."
- A hyphenated word is never split. A single long word that does not fit becomes "...".
- If the width is too small for the ellipsis, still return the ellipsis. The result is never longer than the width, except that the ellipsis itself is kept when the width is smaller than three.

tasks.title: Sentinel members break on copy and pickle
tasks.issue:
Sentinel members such as Sentinel.UNSET do not survive copy, deepcopy, or pickle.

copy.copy(member), copy.deepcopy(member), and pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(member)) must return the same member object. Today the copy is a new object and Sentinel rejects it.

An option created with no default stores UNSET on that default. Copying, deep-copying, or pickling that option must keep a usable option whose default is still the UNSET sentinel.

tasks.title: deprecated label has a stray leading space
tasks.issue:
A deprecated command or option with empty or missing help renders the DEPRECATED label one space too far to the right.

For a command with help "" or help None, and deprecated True or deprecated "USE OTHER COMMAND INSTEAD", the help output contains a line that starts with two spaces then "(DEPRECATED". It must not contain a line that starts with three spaces then "(DEPRECATED".

For an option --foo with help "" or help None:
- deprecated True renders the help record "(DEPRECATED)"
- deprecated "USE B INSTEAD" renders "(DEPRECATED: USE B INSTEAD)"
There is no stray space before the opening parenthesis.

tasks.title: fish completion breaks on multiline help
tasks.issue:
Fish shell completion is broken when help text has more than one line, and the generated fish script is invalid.

A newline inside an option help string must not become a real newline in the fish script. Fish then tries to parse the next line as a new command and completion fails.

Ordinary completion must keep working. For a command with plain choices a and b, where b has the short help "bee":
- an empty current word completes both
- the current word b completes b
- a quoted partial word still completes b

The fish rows use a comma between the type and the value, and a tab before the help. Do not switch that separator to a bare newline.

tasks.title: get_parameter_source is empty during conversion
tasks.issue:
Context.get_parameter_source() returns None inside ParamType.convert and inside eager callbacks. It used to report the real source. This started in 8.4.0.

Repro: a custom type whose convert() returns the value and ctx.get_parameter_source(param.name). An option --default uses that type and default "/tmp/file". An option --nodefault uses that type and has no default.

- With no arguments, --default converts "/tmp/file" and the source is ParameterSource.DEFAULT. --nodefault stays unset.
- With --default cli --nodefault also, both values convert and the source is ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE.

The source must be visible at conversion time. It must not be None.

tasks.title: write_usage prints a blank line when there are no arguments
tasks.issue:
HelpFormatter.write_usage prints a blank line, or stray characters, when there are no arguments.

Wanted results from write_usage:
- prog "Program" and args "" gives "Usage: Program\n"
- the same call with prefix "Run: " gives "Run: Program\n"
- a long prog such as "VeryLongProgramName" on a narrow formatter still gives one line, "Usage: VeryLongProgramName\n", not a second junk line
- prog "Program" and args "[OPTIONS]" gives "Usage: Program [OPTIONS]\n"
- a styled prefix that already contains color codes is kept, and the visible text is "Usage: cli" with no extra trailing space when args is empty

A command named cli with no parameters and options_metavar "" or None prints a help usage line "Usage: cli" with no trailing space.

tasks.title: hidden prompt hides the custom error
tasks.issue:
A prompt with hide_input=True does not show the right error when the value is invalid. The secret the user typed must not appear in the error.

Repro: option --password, prompt=True, hide_input=True. The user types bad.

- type click.INT: the error contains "'***' is not a valid integer" and does not contain bad
- a custom type that fails with "Password must be at least 4 characters" and does not include the raw value: show that message
- a custom type that fails with a message that includes the raw value, such as "rejected: bad": do not show bad. Show "The value you entered was invalid"

tasks.title: a class used as flag_value is constructed too early
tasks.issue:
Using a class as flag_value instantiates that class when the option is filled from the default. The user should get the class object, not an instance.

Repro:

    @click.option("--foo", "ty", flag_value=Foo, type=click.UNPROCESSED, default=True)
    @click.option("--bar", "ty", flag_value=Bar, type=click.UNPROCESSED)

With no arguments, ty is the class Foo, not a Foo instance. Passing --foo or --bar also yields the class.

default=True is what triggers the bad instantiation. default=Foo does not avoid it today; the no-argument result must still be the class.

Also keep default_map rules:
- no default_map and no arguments: the class
- the flag on the command line: the class
- default_map {"value": "from-map"} and no arguments: "from-map"
- default_map {"value": lambda: "lazy-map"} and no arguments: "lazy-map" (the callable in the map is still called)
- default_map {"value": None}: None
- default_map plus the flag on the command line: the class

tasks.title: flag_value is no longer optional
tasks.issue:
An option with is_flag=False and flag_value used to accept the bare flag and use flag_value. Since 8.3.0 the bare flag errors with "Option '--name' requires an argument."

    @click.option("--name", is_flag=False, flag_value="Flag", default="Default")

- no arguments: Hello, Default!
- --name with no value: Hello, Flag!
- --name Ada: Hello, Ada!

The same pattern with type=int must convert flag_value. --count with is_flag=False, flag_value="1", type=int, default=0, and a command that prints one line per count, prints "Line 1" when the user passes bare --count.

tasks.title: default=True on shared flags depends on declaration order
zsh completion breaks when a value contains a colon
tasks.issue:
Zsh completion does not escape a colon inside a completion value.

Zsh uses a colon to split a value from its description. A colon in the value must be escaped only when that item has a description. A colon in the description stays as it is. A value with a colon and no description must stay literal, because escaping it would change the value.

Example: value "c:d" with description "cee: dee" is emitted with the value written as c\:d. Value "c:e" with no description stays c:e.

tasks.title: shell completion drops commands inside nested groups
tasks.issue:
Shell completion does not offer commands once a group is nested inside another group.

Shape: top group cli, child group get, grandchild group full with option --verbose, and command data under full with option -a.

Completions:
- no words yet: get
- after get: full
- after get full: data
- after get full, current word starts with "-": --verbose and --help
- after get full data: no commands
- after get full data, current word starts with "-": -a and --help

tasks.title: boolean flags get the wrong value when a type is set
tasks.issue:
A flag with is_flag=True and an explicit boolean type does not get the flag value.

For option --foo, is_flag=True:
- type bool, omitted: False. Passed: True.
- type bool and default True, omitted: True. Passed: False.
- the same two rows for type click.BOOL
- type str, omitted: an empty string. Passed: the string True

Also, a normal option (not a flag) whose default object raises ValueError from __bool__ must still run when the option is omitted. It must not crash.

tasks.title: generated help option is not eager
tasks.issue:
A help option created from help_option_names is not eager, so callbacks run in the wrong order and help does not win.

Command context_settings help_option_names is ("--my-help",). Option -a is a flag whose callback prints "Value of a is: True" and then exits. Option -b is the same but is_eager=True.

- --my-help alone prints help and does not print the -a or -b value line. Exit code 0.
- -a alone prints the -a value line and does not print help.
- -a -b prints the -b value line only, because -b is eager.
- -a --my-help and --my-help -a both print help and do not print the -a value line.
- -b --my-help prints the -b value line and does not print help, because both are eager and -b came first.
- --my-help -b prints help and does not print the -b value line. Help is eager and came first.

Today the last case runs -b instead of help.

tasks.title: close callbacks do not run when the command exits
tasks.issue:
Context.call_on_close callbacks do not run when the command exits through ctx.exit(). Cleanup is skipped. In a long-lived process that calls exit without killing the interpreter, state leaks.

A command that sets ctx.obj, registers a close callback, and then calls ctx.exit() must run that callback before it returns. The callback must still see the current context and the obj that was set. The command must not print text that comes after exit.

If one option registers a close callback and another option calls ctx.exit(), the close callback for an option that already ran must still run. If the exiting option is eager and runs first, callbacks that belong to options that did not run must not run.
